title: Delaunay Hull
comment: Delaunay Hull — The Delaunay triangulation in d dimensions can be obtained by computing the convex hull on a paraboloid lifting in d+1 dimensions. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delaunay_triangulation#d-dimensional_Delaunay

title: Krigging
comment: Krigging — Kriging (also known as Wiener interpolation) is a method for kernel interpolation that accounts for uncertainty using Gaussian processes. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kriging
alt_text: Krigging. Kriging (also known as Wiener interpolation) is a method for kernel interpolation that accounts for uncertainty using Gaussian processes.

title: L1 Norm
comment: L1 Norm — The l1 norm provides an optimal balance between convexity and sparsity. It is used in various applications including the lasso and basis pursuit denoising, pioneered by David Donoho and Robert Tibshirani. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basis_pursuit_denoising
alt_text: L1 Norm. The l1 norm provides an optimal balance between convexity and sparsity. It is used in various applications including the lasso and basis pursuit denoising, pioneered by David Donoho and Robert Tibshirani.

title: Oscillator
comment: Oscillator — The harmonic oscillator is the canonical linear second order ODE. Parametrized by a single damping parameter. Solutions are (possibly complex) exponentials. Interpolates between periodic motion and exponential decay. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harmonic_oscillator
alt_text: Oscillator. The harmonic oscillator is the canonical linear second order ODE. Parametrized by a single damping parameter. Solutions are (possibly complex) exponentials. Interpolates between periodic motion and exponential decay.

title: Voltera Lotka
comment: Voltera Lotka — Lotka-Volterra equations is a non-linear 2D ODE modeling prey/predator behaviors which exhibits periodic solutions. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lotka%E2%80%93Volterra_equations
alt_text: Voltera Lotka. Lotka-Volterra equations is a non-linear 2D ODE modeling prey/predator behaviors which exhibits periodic solutions.

title: Heavy Ball
comment: Heavy Ball — Poljak heavy ball method speeds up gradient descent by introducing momentum. Corresponding to second order ODEs. https://distill.pub/2017/momentum/
alt_text: Heavy Ball. Poljak heavy ball method speeds up gradient descent by introducing momentum. Corresponding to second order ODEs.

title: Periodic Motions
comment: Periodic Motions — Only harmonic spring and gravity central forces produce periodic motions. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bertrand%27s_theorem
alt_text: Periodic Motions. Only harmonic spring and gravity central forces produce periodic motions.

title: Kernel Domain
comment: Kernel Domain — The kernel of a domain is the (convex) set of locations from which you can see all other locations in the domain. It is the intersections of all half-planes tangent to the shape. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star-shaped_polygon
alt_text: Kernel Domain. The kernel of a domain is the (convex) set of locations from which you can see all other locations in the domain. It is the intersections of all half-planes tangent to the shape.

title: John Ellipsoid
comment: John Ellipsoid — John's and Lowner's ellipsoids are polar one from each others. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_ellipsoid
alt_text: John Ellipsoid. John's and Lowner's ellipsoids are polar one from each others.

title: Sobolev Ball
comment: Sobolev Ball — A Sobolev ball is an ellipsoid in infinite dimension aligned along the Fourier axes. A random Sobolev function has a Fourier transform with random phase. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sobolev_space
alt_text: Sobolev Ball. A Sobolev ball is an ellipsoid in infinite dimension aligned along the Fourier axes. A random Sobolev function has a Fourier transform with random phase.

title: Denoising Flows
comment: Denoising Flows — The gradient flow of the Dirichlet energy is the heat equation, which blur edges. The total variation flow makes the image cartoon-like, and requires some care to be defined and implemented (division by 0 when the gradient vanishes). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heat_equation
alt_text: Denoising Flows. The gradient flow of the Dirichlet energy is the heat equation, which blur edges. The total variation flow makes the image cartoon-like, and requires some care to be defined and implemented (division by 0 when the gradient vanishes).

title: Co Area
comment: Co Area — The co-area formula relates the total variation to the perimeters of the level set. Can be extended to (possibly) discontinuous functions of bounded total variation. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coarea_formula
alt_text: Co Area. The co-area formula relates the total variation to the perimeters of the level set. Can be extended to (possibly) discontinuous functions of bounded total variation.

title: Logistic Map
comment: Logistic Map — The logistic map can have complex patterns of adherence points depending on the value of its scale parameter r. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Logistic_map
alt_text: Logistic Map. The logistic map can have complex patterns of adherence points depending on the value of its scale parameter r.

title: Helmoltz Decomposition
comment: Helmoltz Decomposition — The Helmholtz-Hodge decomposition split vectors fields in two orthogonal subspaces: incompressible and irrotational. In 2-D, corresponds to the sum of a gradient field and a rotated gradient field. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helmholtz_decomposition
alt_text: Helmoltz Decomposition. The Helmholtz-Hodge decomposition split vectors fields in two orthogonal subspaces: incompressible and irrotational. In 2-D, corresponds to the sum of a gradient field and a rotated gradient field.

title: Mean Shift
comment: Mean Shift — The mean-shift algorithm is a clustering method that progressively evolves points toward local maximum of a kernel density estimator. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mean_shift
alt_text: Mean Shift. The mean-shift algorithm is a clustering method that progressively evolves points toward local maximum of a kernel density estimator.
